intro: A fairly quiet day. AI agents that shop for people (Google Gemini Tasks, Daydream) and fresh data on AI search cutting clicks lead. Instagram's Amazon links story is still rolling through follow-up coverage.

must_reads.title: Google expands access to Gemini Tasks, which can help with calls, purchases
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Google's assistant can now make purchases for people, so more buying will start inside AI tools instead of on a creator's link. Links need to keep working, and keep getting credit, when an agent is doing the clicking.

must_reads.title: Google's AI Mode cuts clicks to websites by 18.8 points, field test finds
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: a field test puts a number on how much Google's AI Mode cuts clicks to websites. Creators and publishers who rely on search will get fewer visits, so every click they do get has to count.

must_reads.title: Twitch’s shoppable ads put the Amazon basket one tap from the stream
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Amazon now has a paid route from Twitch streams straight to its basket, the same week Instagram opened Amazon links. Amazon is building its own paths from every platform, which raises the value of one link that works across all of them.

must_reads.title: WeShop Launches US Shopping App With Seven Affiliate Networks
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: a new US shopping app launched with seven affiliate networks and 750+ retailers. Affiliate money keeps spreading across many networks and apps, so creators need links that work whichever retailer or network sits behind them.

must_reads.title: Daydream’s new AI agent acts as your personal stylist — and can shop for you, too
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: a second AI shopping agent this week can remember taste, track sales and check out for the user. Shopping agents are moving from demo to product, and links will increasingly be read by machines as well as people.
